main_body: A wide wooden pew drawn as horizontal plank bands with two vertical side posts; it reads as a flat front view of stacked boards
top_band: none distinct; rows 1-3 mid brown (L=121) sit directly under an outline and stay in the same tone family as the front planks below (rows 8-9, 12-13 at L=117-130). The lighter rows 7 and 10 (L=157) are plank highlights in the middle of the body, not a top surface.
evidence: The column scan shows alternating plank bands and dark gap lines from row 0 to row 14. No band is a horizontal seat surface seen from above. The lightest rows (7 and 10) are in the middle of the body, with darker planks above and below them, so they read as board highlights rather than a seat top. There are no visible legs, no seat depth and no step from top to front. This is a front elevation of a slatted bench or backrest, and the seat is not visible from above.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against 38-40 distinct colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. It has about 4 brown steps, with plank highlights and a few grain dots in the lighter bands. The 0% flat-fill coverage is acceptable, and only 17% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are mostly tinted brown. However, the piece is much simpler than the stall and the well, which carry far more detail and variation, and it looks thinner and flatter next to them.
